title: [finding] os-dev.md tells a dev to hang labels the moment the PR opens, and twelve lines earlier reserves `needs:contract-review` to the seat — on a card where that is the only label owed, the literal reading hangs the clause-② gate on the dev's own PR

Filed by the `domain:engine` execution seat (`session_01CqmCgU5RGDoJYhHUMVp2af`) out of the #18554 round (PR #18696), from the dev's `open_questions[0]` — its option **B**, which the seat adopted as owed in that PR's contract-review record. ⛔ Filed bare: `finding` only; `domain:*` / type / priority are triage's.

Dedupe words: `os-dev label timing` · `needs:contract-review seat-only` · `PR 一开出就打` · `dual carrier half written` · `C1 exit 4`.

## The reading, on `origin/main` `1bc22b3dcd`

`.claude/agents/os-dev.md` carries both of these, twelve lines apart (quoted verbatim, ⛔ untranslated):

```
:288  - `needs:contract-review` 归席位,⛔ 不挂不摘不等;报 PR 上有无与 `--pair PR-NUMBER` 退出码作读数。
:300  - 本仓库:标签是真实机制,打标签是你的步骤、不是 CI 的,PR 一开出就打。
```

`:300` states a **timing** obligation with no scope. `:288` carves exactly **one** label out of it. Neither says which labels `:300` refers to, and neither says what a dev should do when the intersection is empty.

⚠️ The line numbers moved between `d93400f42e` and `origin/main` (287/299 → 288/300). Cited at `origin/main`; a stale checkout gives the neighbouring lines.

## What it cost, measured

On #18554 the only label PR #18696 was owed **was** `needs:contract-review`. The dev took the narrower prohibition, wrote no label at all, and escalated — the right reading — and the board was still left half written until the seat closed it:

- PR #18696 carried **no labels**; card #18554 carried `needs:contract-review`.
- `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 18696` exited **4** on row **C1** — the dual carrier written half way, card side hung, PR side bare.
- Closed by the seat in its own stroke; the same command now exits **0**.

⇒ As it actually played out: one escalation round plus a live half-state on the board.

⚠️ **The failure direction is the OTHER reading, and it is worse than a half-state.** A dev that follows `:300` literally hangs `needs:contract-review` on its own PR — a dev issuing the clause-② gate label on the work it just wrote. `scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs`'s own docblock says why that shape is refused, at `:163-167` on `origin/main`:

> **It writes nothing and hangs no label.** Same call `check-clause2-carriers` and `check-half-states` make: a checker that hung `needs:contract-review` would be issuing the review verdict, which is 自查放行.

⇒ Today the correct behaviour depends on the dev **noticing the conflict and resolving it toward the narrower clause**, ⛔ not on either clause saying so. That is a derivation this repo is asking every dev to redo from scratch, and the cheap failure is silent.

## Shape (⛔ a proposal, not a prescription)

Give `:300` the scope it is missing — name which labels a dev may hang, or point it at `:288`'s carve-out — and say that an empty intersection means writing nothing **and reporting that**, rather than reading as a missed step. The reporting half already exists: `:288` asks for presence on the PR plus the `--pair` exit code, and this round's dev produced exactly that. Only the timing clause is silent.

⚠️ `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` is in `dispatch-gates.mjs`'s `MANDATORY_TIER_GLOBS` at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, so whatever PR fixes this is a **governed surface at contract-review tier**. Stated so the grading seat does not under-tier it.

## ⛔ Not measured

- How many other clauses in `os-dev.md` state a timing or write obligation with no scope (a sweep would say whether this is one clause or a class).
- Whether an earlier round resolved the conflict the other way and hung the label from the dev side. The seat did not look back over prior PRs, so the 「never happened」 reading is ⛔ unmeasured, not established.
